title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles
abstract: arXiv:2611.33519v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: AI coding agents increasingly write and submit code with limited human review, and much of it passes functional tests while remaining insecure. We show that these failures persist. Across 14 task sequences, Codex, Claude Code, and Qwen Code fixed a vulnerability 85.7% of the time when shown the failing security test, then reintroduced the same vulnerability class in a new session 26.7% of the time, about as often as agents that had never seen it (27.5%). The capability is present; the retention is not. Neither recording the repair in the agent's persistent context nor supplying published secure coding principles closed the gap: the recorded fix stayed tied to the family of the task it came from, and the principles, written for human developers, remained too general to apply to the code at hand. The knowledge exists; it is not activated. We call the missing ability security self-improvement: an agent learns from its own security failure

translated_title: PRECEPT：通过演进式原则实现编码智能体的安全自我改进
translated_abstract: AI 编码智能体越来越多地在有限人工审查的情况下编写和提交代码，其中许多代码虽然通过了功能测试，但仍然不安全。我们证明这些失败会持续存在。在 14 个任务序列中，Codex、Claude Code 和 Qwen Code 在看到失败的安全测试时能以 85.7% 的概率修复漏洞，但在新的会话中有 26.7% 的概率重新引入同类漏洞，这与从未见过该漏洞的智能体的频率相当（27.5%）。能力是存在的，但保留并不存在。无论是将修复记录在智能体的持久上下文中，还是向其提供已发布的安全编码原则，都无法弥补这一差距：记录下来的修复仍然局限于其来源任务所属的系列，而这些为人类开发者撰写的原则仍然过于宽泛，无法应用于手头的代码。知识是存在的，但没有被激活。我们将这种缺失的能力称为安全自我改进：智能体能够从自身的安全失败中学习
tldr: 论文揭示当前编码智能体虽能修复安全漏洞却无法在新会话中保留并激活相关安全知识，并据此提出 PRECEPT 框架，通过不断演进的通用安全原则实现编码智能体的安全自我改进。
en_tdlr: The paper reveals that coding agents can fix vulnerabilities but fail to retain and activate that security knowledge across sessions, and proposes PRECEPT, a framework enabling security self-improvement of coding agents through evolving generalizable security principles.
